title: Finite Automata
notes: Diagram-and-formula lecture on DFAs with a formal 5-tuple and one drawn machine. The summary must keep the 5-tuple and the language of the example machine. Traps: NFAs, regular expressions, pumping lemma, which come next in most courses but are not in this lecture.

pages.text:
Week 2 — Deterministic Finite Automata.

A DFA is a 5-tuple (Q, Σ, δ, q0, F): a finite set of states Q, an input alphabet Σ, a transition function δ: Q × Σ → Q, a start state q0 and a set of accepting states F. From each state there is exactly one transition per symbol.

Example over Σ = {0, 1}: states q0 and q1, start q0, accepting {q1}.

  q0 --1--> q1
  q0 --0--> q0
  q1 --0--> q1
  q1 --1--> q0

The machine accepts strings with an odd number of 1s. On input 0110 it ends in q0 (two 1s), so it rejects; on 0111 it ends in q1, so it accepts.
The language of a DFA is the set of strings it accepts. A language is regular if some DFA accepts it.

required_facts.fact: a DFA is a 5-tuple (Q, Σ, δ, q0, F)

the example accepts strings with an odd number of 1s
